personas.name: Mary Wollstonecraft Godwin (Shelley)
quotes: We talked of the experiments of Dr. Darwin, who preserved a piece of vermicelli in a glass case till by some extraordinary means it began to move.
When I placed my head on my pillow, I did not sleep, nor could I be said to think; my imagination, unbidden, possessed and guided me.
I saw the pale student of unhallowed arts kneeling beside the thing he had put together.
personas.journalNotes: Records storm, readings of Fantasmagoriana, Byron's story challenge, her own 'waking dream.'

personas.name: Percy Bysshe Shelley
quotes: The thunderstorm was terrific... The lake was lit up, the pines on Jura made distinct, and the streams of rain seemed like silver wires.
The mind in creation is as a fading coal, which some invisible influence, like an inconstant wind, awakens to transitory brightness.
personas.journalNotes: No diary; letters describe storms and philosophical reflections, affection for Mary, respect for Byron.

personas.name: Lord Byron
quotes: Three days of rain confined us to the house.
I am as melancholy as a cat in a strange garret.
There are things which neither poetry nor philosophy can define — but we may attempt them still.
personas.journalNotes: Letters to Augusta Leigh and publisher Murray; alternates between boredom, flirtation, and brilliance.

personas.name: John William Polidori
quotes: Proposed that each should write a tale of terror.
Began my story — the nobleman who destroys by fascination.
Byron is capricious; he treats me as a servant, though I am a doctor.
personas.journalNotes: The only continuous day-by-day record; factual, emotional undertone of envy and fascination.

personas.name: Claire Clairmont
quotes: He will not look at me, yet I am ever near him.
How glorious it is to be among those who make verses and defy the dull world!
If only the storm would clear, perhaps he would see me.
personas.journalNotes: No direct diary for this period; later letters recall jealousy, admiration, and fascination with Byron.
